title: Set-generated cocomplete preaisles of derived module sheaves
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,J)$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of rings on it, with module-sheaf category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Work in the unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], in one fixed universe. Let $S$ be a set of objects of $D(\mathcal A)$. Let $\mathcal U$ be the smallest strictly full subcategory containing $S$ and zero and closed under small coproducts, direct summands, the shift $[1]$, and extensions (if $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ is distinguished and $A,C\in\mathcal U$, then $B\in\mathcal U$). Put $\mathcal U^\perp=\{B:\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=0\text{ for every }A\in\mathcal U\}$. Then every $K\in D(\mathcal A)$ admits a distinguished triangle $A\to K\to B\to A[1]$ with $A\in\mathcal U$ and $B\in\mathcal U^\perp$. Equivalently, $(\mathcal U,\mathcal U^\perp[1])$ is a t-structure [def-weil-t-structure]. Moreover $B\in\mathcal U^\perp$ if and only if $\operatorname{Hom}(G[k],B)=0$ for all $G\in S$ and all integers $k\geq0$.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is Grothendieck abelian, without requiring $R$ commutative. Choose a generator $U$. Use [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] for the small coproducts in $D(\mathcal A)$; these are the images of termwise coproducts. All sets, ordinals and Hom sets below are in the fixed indexing universe. Choose a representing complex $P_G$ for each $G\in S$, possible because derived localization has complexes as its objects [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Grothendieck module category and termwise coproduct setup; Stacks derived.tex Tag 07D9, via the cited nodes

proof.text: Choose $\kappa$ from [lem-pur-kinjective-acyclic-quotient-complexes-bounded-size]. By [lem-pur-kinjective-set-iso-classes-bounded-size], representatives of objects having subobject-size at most $\kappa$ form a set. Integer-indexed choices of these representatives and choices of their differentials form a set, since every Hom is a set. Taking those satisfying the complex, bounded-above and acyclicity conditions gives a set $\mathcal M$ representing every bounded-above acyclic complex with term sizes at most $\kappa$. The subobjects $N\subseteq U$ likewise form a set by [lem-pur-kinjective-set-of-subobjects]. For an object $V$ define $D^n(V)$ to have $V$ in degrees $n,n+1$, differential $1_V$, and zero elsewhere. Define a set $J$ of monomorphisms of complexes consisting of $D^n(N)\hookrightarrow D^n(U)$ for all these $N,n$, and $M\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cone}(1_M)$ for $M\in\mathcal M$. The latter is the inclusion of the unshifted summand under the cone convention [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Each cokernel of a map in $J$ is acyclic: it is respectively the contractible disk $D^n(U/N)$, or $M[1]$.

source.place: Tags 079K (lemma-acyclic-quotient-complexes-bounded-size), 079E (lemma-set-iso-classes-bounded-size), 0E8N (lemma-set-of-subobjects); explicit disk and cone test maps

proof.text: Suppose a complex $I$ has the extension property against $J$: every chain map from a domain in $J$ to $I$ extends across its codomain. A chain map $D^n(V)\to I$ is uniquely a map $V\to I^n$, with its degree $n+1$ component forced to be $d_I^n$ times that map. The disk tests therefore say that every $N\to I^n$ extends to $U$. By [lem-pur-kinjective-characterize-injective], all $I^n$ are injective. The other tests make every map $M\to I$ extend over $\operatorname{Cone}(1_M)$, hence nullhomotopic, because the identity cone is contractible (the off-diagonal identity gives its contracting homotopy). Transporting across the chosen complex isomorphisms gives this for every bounded-above acyclic complex of term size at most $\kappa$. Thus [lem-pur-kinjective-characterize-K-injective], with both bounded-size hypotheses supplied by the choice of $\kappa$, makes $I$ K-injective.

Enlarge $J$ to a set $I_S$ by adjoining $P_G[k]\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Cone}(1_{P_G[k]})$ for every $G\in S$ and integer $k\geq0$. All are monomorphisms. Choose an uncountable regular cardinal $\mu$ greater than the subobject-size of every degree of every domain in $I_S$; there are only a set of such degrees. For a continuous $\mu$-chain of monomorphisms of complexes, [prop-pur-kinjective-objects-small] factors each component of a map from one of these domains through a stage. The supremum of the countably many stages is below $\mu$; at a common stage the components commute with the differentials because the maps from that stage to the colimit are monic. The same monicity makes two chain maps equal at a common stage whenever they have equal colimit images. Thus Hom from every domain preserves these chain colimits. Coproducts of monomorphisms are monic: finite sums are exact, and the arbitrary sum is their filtered colimit, exact by AB5. Pushouts preserve monomorphisms in an abelian category, and AB5 preserves monomorphisms at limit stages. Consequently all $I_S$-cell chains meet this smallness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 079F (proposition-objects-are-small), with componentwise chain-map argument; AB5 in the Grothendieck definition

proof.text: Represent the given $K$ by a complex $K_0$. Complexes have small colimits computed degreewise: take the colimit of the terms and induce the differentials from their compatible structure maps, obtaining $d^2=0$ and the colimit universal property degreewise. Hence [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] applies to $I_S$ with the regular cardinal just chosen. Factor $K_0\to0$ as $K_0\hookrightarrow I\to0$, with the first map an $I_S$-cell map and the second having right lifting against $I_S$. Write the cell chain as $(K_\beta)_{\beta\leq\theta}$, starting at $K_0$ and ending at $I$. All its maps are degreewise monic by the preceding step. Its successor cokernels are coproducts of the cokernels of the attached maps: pushout of a monomorphism preserves its cokernel, and coproducts preserve cokernels by their universal property. Thus they are coproducts of acyclic complexes and complexes $P_G[k+1]$, $k\geq0$.

source.place: Small-object argument (existing Mathlib leaf) with the explicitly verified smallness and cocompleteness hypotheses

proof.text: Put $E_\beta=(K_\beta/K_0)[-1]$ as a complex. These form a continuous chain of monomorphisms with $E_0=0$; quotient by the fixed subcomplex commutes with the limit colimits since cokernels are colimits. Its successor quotients are the preceding successor cokernels shifted by $[-1]$. Their derived images lie in $\mathcal U$: the shifted acyclic summands become zero, and $Q(P_G[k+1][-1])\cong G[k]\in\mathcal U$. Termwise coproducts give derived coproducts by [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts]. Apply [lem-per-preaisle-transfinite-monomorphism-closure] to this filtration and $\mathcal U$, which has exactly its required zero, extension, positive-shift and coproduct closure. We get $A:=Q((I/K_0)[-1])\in\mathcal U$. Applying the lemma to this shifted quotient filtration is essential: it does not assume that $\mathcal U$ is closed under $[-1]$.

source.place: Cell-filtration quotient calculation and transfinite preaisle closure; agent argument

proof.text: Right lifting of $I\to0$ against $J$ is exactly the extension property of Step 3, so $I$ is K-injective. Right lifting against the additional identity-cone inclusions says every chain map $P_G[k]\to I$ extends across its contractible identity cone, and is therefore nullhomotopic. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the homotopy-to-derived Hom map with target $I$ is bijective, with no boundedness hypothesis on $P_G[k]$. Thus $B:=QI$ satisfies $\operatorname{Hom}(G[k],B)=0$ for all $G\in S$, $k\geq0$.

source.place: derived.tex Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), with the explicit cone-extension nullhomotopy test

proof.text: For any $B$ satisfying the generator vanishing, define $\mathcal W_B=\{X:\operatorname{Hom}(X[k],B)=0\text{ for all }k\geq0\}$. It contains zero and $S$, is strictly full, and is closed under $[1]$. It is closed under small coproducts since shifting commutes with coproducts (the shift has its inverse as an adjoint) and Hom out of a coproduct is the product of Hom sets. It is closed under summands by composing with the splitting maps. For a distinguished $X\to Y\to Z\to X[1]$ with $X,Z\in\mathcal W_B$, any $Y[k]\to B$ restricts to zero on $X[k]$, so factors through $Z[k]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact], and is zero. Therefore $\mathcal U\subseteq\mathcal W_B$ by the defining minimality of $\mathcal U$, and $B\in\mathcal U^\perp$. Conversely, $G[k]\in\mathcal U$ for $G\in S$, $k\geq0$, so every $B\in\mathcal U^\perp$ satisfies the generator vanishing. This proves the full stated generator test and applies in particular to the $B$ constructed above.

source.place: derived.tex Tag 0149 (lemma-representable-homological), contravariant Hom exactness; orthogonal closure argument

proof.text: The short exact sequence of complexes $0\to K_0\to I\to I/K_0\to0$ gives a quasi-isomorphism $\operatorname{Cone}(K_0\to I)\to I/K_0$ by [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso]. The cone-triangle convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and its inverse rotation therefore give a distinguished triangle $A\to K\to B\to A[1]$, with the $A$ of Step 6 and the $B$ of Step 7. We have proved $A\in\mathcal U$ and $B\in\mathcal U^\perp$. Finally $\mathcal U[1]\subseteq\mathcal U$ by definition, and $\mathcal U^\perp[-1]\subseteq\mathcal U^\perp$ since $\operatorname{Hom}(X,B[-1])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(X[1],B)=0$ for $X\in\mathcal U$. Hence $\mathcal U^\perp\subseteq\mathcal U^\perp[1]$, the required lower-class shift condition. Orthogonality is its defining vanishing, and the constructed triangle is the remaining axiom of [def-weil-t-structure] for $(\mathcal U,\mathcal U^\perp[1])$.

Cone extension is the same as a null-homotopy, so 079L applies with both size hypotheses from 079K. (4) componentwise 079F smallness holds at an uncountable regular μ. Monos are preserved by coproducts (AB4), pushouts and limit stages (AB5), so the hypothesis of the small-object leaf holds.
